test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

For better or (for) worse

options.text: To accept whatever results; good or bad

solution: The correct answer is** ****"To accept whatever results; good or bad."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The phrase** "for better or (for) worse" **is often used in the context of wedding vows or commitments, expressing a willingness to endure both positive and negative circumstances that may arise in a relationship or situation. (वाक्यांश "for better or (for) worse" का उपयोग अक्सर शादी की प्रतिज्ञा या प्रतिबद्धताओं के संदर्भ में किया जाता है, जो किसी रिश्ते या स्थिति में उत्पन्न होने वाली सकारात्मक और नकारात्मक दोनों परिस्थितियों को सहन करने की इच्छा व्यक्त करता है।) • It implies a commitment to stay together or persevere through good and bad times, regardless of the challenges that may come. • **Example**: *We promised to be there for each other, for better or worse.* • Hence, option 2 is the correct answer. 167:T998, Here, the erroneous part is** "was record breaking."**
